newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan hog epidemic slows, but new disease feared.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan hog epidemic slows, but new disease feared.

text.p: The spread of hog foot-and-mouth epidemic in Taiwan has slowed, but farm officials on Thursday feared an outbreak of a chicken deadly disease.
"The foot and mouth disease is still spreading, but at a slower speed," Chen Jung-jang, an official with the Council of Agriculture, told Reuters by telephone.
But the council said on Wednesday it had heard reports that a new disease was beginning to infect chicken farms, although it could not confirm the reports.
"We have sent some sick chickens for lab tests and are waiting for the results," a council official told Reuters by telephone.
Taiwan currently has about 118 million chickens, raised mostly for domestic consumption.
Data from the council showed that, as of Tuesday, the airborne hog foot-and-mouth virus has been detected on 4,539 of Taiwan's 25,000 hog farms, up from 3,422 farms a week ago.
The latest official projection forecast that over 3.54 million of the island's 14 million pigs have been or would have to be destroyed.
The disease spread into eastern Taiwan in the Taitung county for the first time on Wednesday, prompting the council to close the area's hog wholesale centres for five days.
The northeastern Hualien county is only area of Taiwan still free of foot and mouth disease.
Taiwan banned pork exports on March 20 and ordered a mass slaughter and inoculation drive after detecting the epidemic at nine hog farms.
Taiwan lifted the export ban on April 17, but exporters were required to obtain permits from importing countries.
So far all of Taiwan's previous export targets, including Japan and South Korea, have refused to buy Taiwan pork.
